top.title: Who will step up to preserve space age artefacts for future generations?
top.description: NASA/JPL-Caltech Around 40,000 years from now, the Voyager 1 probe will pass within astronomical spitting distance of the star Gliese 445. From there, it will continue drifting through the universe on an endless journey that marks humanity’s first attempt to reach the stars. Voyager 1 – which on 18 November will have travelled one light day from Earth – began its odyssey almost 50 years ago, meaning it has been operating for the majority of the space age. That makes it a rarity: most of our iconic spacecraft ended their lives burned up in Earth’s atmosphere or in bits at the bottom of the ocean. Two of the most important missions still flying today, the Hubble Space Telescope and the International Space Station, look set to share the same fate in the near future, even as scientists call for Hubble to be preserved . While some craft like the space shuttles are on display in museums, our present space history is, essentially, in its dark ages, with little thought currently given to preserving spacecraft in situ, where our space-travelling descendants may wish to marvel at them. Even the Apollo hardware left behind on the moon has almost no protection in international law. Advertisement Perhaps we need an organisation like the UNESCO World Heritage Committee to designate important space artefacts for preservation, and encourage funding from cultural and heritage budgets, not scientific ones, to do this. Of course, with such budgets often under threat and the US set to leave UNESCO at the end of this year, this could introduce new problems. Private philanthropy is another option. If humanity is to one day take its place among the stars, a fantasy that fuels many a tech billionaire, it would be a great shame to not be able to look back at how we got there. Just as we remember 19th-century captains of industry like Andrew Carnegie and J. P. Morgan for funding great cultural institutions, perhaps we should be lobbying for the creation of a Musk Space Museum or Bezos Orbital Institute.

top.title: Killer Bigfoot evidence rejected by Bigfoot’s biggest fans
top.description: Josie Ford Feedback is our weekly column of bizarre stories, implausible advertising claims, confusing instructions and more Caught on camera One of the defining features of conspiracy theories is that they are “self-sealing”. If you confront a conspiracy theorist with the lack of evidence for their claim, they will turn this back on you and argue that this very lack of evidence is proof of how powerful the conspiracy is. This is foreshadowing. Advertisement Feedback is interested in watching the new documentary Capturing Bigfoot . We can’t, because we live in the UK and it isn’t available here , but if anyone would care to rectify that, we will stick ourselves in front of it immediately. The film is about the classic footage that purports to show a Bigfoot loping alongside a river in California. Shot by Roger Patterson and Robert Gimlin in 1967, the clip became one of the canonical pieces of evidence for the existence of Bigfoot: a mythical humanoid that supposedly lives in the forests of North America. Bigfoot is one of the icons of cryptozoology, the search for probably-nonexistent creatures. It has hordes of devotees. In Capturing Bigfoot , film-maker Marq Evans uncovers what really happened in 1967. He speaks to Patterson’s associate Bob Heironimus, who says he wore an ape costume in the footage. Crucially, Evans also finds a lost piece of 16-millimetre film, shot in 1966, showing a rehearsal for the final Patterson-Gimlin video. A review of the documentary in Variety calls this footage “the smoking gun”. It is, Feedback would suggest, a case no defence lawyer could wriggle out of. So, the Patterson-Gimlin film purporting to show Bigfoot was fake. Feedback and our editor worried if we were legally safe saying that, but then, as our editor said, “come on”. It is perhaps telling that, when we mentioned this to Mrs Feedback, her response was “I could have sworn I already knew that”. Indeed, these accusations have been made before, notably in Greg Long’s 2004 book The Making of Bigfoot . The new thing is that rehearsal footage. Naturally, then, this footage is what the Bigfoot Field Researchers Organization pushed back on. Its president is quoted in The Times as saying: “My initial reaction is, how could you believe that in the age of AI?… Even if they found some reel, how would you know whether what they’re showing in the documentary is what’s on the reel?” And thus the foreshadowing pays off. top.title: Extraordinary image of bioluminescent plankton captured by photographer
top.description: Lucifer’s Vortex by Tom Fecht Tom Fecht On the edge of twilight, the surface of the sea glows. Millions of tiny dots produce an eerie blue light, barely visible to humans. Each one is a single plankton shining with bioluminescence, and the dots’ light blurs together as the waters churn around them. Tom Fecht captured this image in Brittany, France, looking down into the Atlantic Ocean under a bright moon. The luminescence of the plankton is dim, so his first attempts to catch it resulted in nothing but darkness. “I figured something must be going on which you couldn’t see with the naked eye, so I just blindly started opening the shutter every time a wave broke,” says Fecht. Finally, he captured the light from the plankton mixing with reflections of moonlight in a churning wave. He titled the image Lucifer’s Vortex after the compounds, called luciferins, that generate this light. While these plankton aren’t officially endangered – no plankton species is, in part due to the impossibility of tracking them individually – their future is highly uncertain. Warmer waters force them to migrate polewards and, in some places, die off, their access to nutrients blocked by changing ocean currents. Advertisement The word “luciferin” comes from the Latin for “light-bringer”, and Fecht hopes the plankton’s otherworldly glow also brings light to the plight they face. “If you want to engage in protecting nature, you first of all need an understanding of its beauty,” he says. This image is part of the touring Storm exhibition from the Prix Pictet award, on view at Fotografiska Shenzhen in China until 29 November.

top.title: Ayra Starr Joins Coachella 2027 Lineup Alongside SZA, Dua Lipa & More
top.description: Ayra Starr returns with her third studio album, Starrgirl. Ayra Starr is taking her global run to another big stage! The Nigerian singer has been named among the performers at Coachella 2027, adding another major festival appearance to her growing list of international milestones. The Beninese-born singer, who rose to prominence as one of Afrobeats’ leading voices after joining Mavin Records, is set to perform on both weekends of the festival, Sunday, April 11, and Sunday, April 18, 2027. Coachella will take place at the Empire Polo Club in Indio, California. It’s been a big year for Ayra, with her third studio album, Starrgirl, adding to an already exciting run. Fans heading to the festival can look forward to hearing songs from the project, including “ Tornado ” and “ Midnight in New York “, as well as her collaboration “ Gimme Dat “. There’s also room for crowd favourites such as “ Rush “, “ Commas ” and “ Heaven Baby “. Ayra shares the Sunday bill with headliner SZA , alongside Victoria Monét , Jorja Smith , Becky G and Don Toliver . The wider festival, running from April 9 to 11 and April 16 to 18, will also feature headliners Dua Lipa and Tame Impala , with Madonna set for a special appearance in the dance tent. Her Coachella booking follows another major moment in London, where she performed at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium as part of the NFL International Games halftime show, becoming the first African artist to headline the show. And there’s even more for fans to look forward to. Ayra has announced her 20-city Starrgirl World Tour, which will take her across Europe and North America in early 2027 before she heads to the California desert for Coachella. top.title: Beyond The Sole: How Nigerian Artist Eugene Is Turning Waste Into Beauty For A Better World
top.description: An art project that started as a final-year assessment at Auchi Polytechnic, Auchi, Edo State, Nigeria, has turned into a full-time career for Konboye Eugene. In his studio in Kuto, Abeokuta, Ogun State, the Nigerian artist is giving discarded footwear a new lease of life, transforming them into colourful portraits. “I’ve been a full-time studio practitioner for about seven years now. I started when I was in my final year at Auchi Polytechnic, where I studied painting,” Eugene said. “It started as an assignment for me when I was in school. But over the course of my practice, I have become a bit more environmentally aware.” ﻿ Statistics cited by Green Network Asia indicate that over 200 million pairs of flip-flops are discarded each year globally, contributing significantly to plastic and rubber pollution in landfills and oceans. Materials ‘Everywhere, Anywhere’ Eugene’s craft draws attention to the environmental impact of discarded footwear and the need for better ways to manage waste. “I source my material through landfills, the streets, literally everywhere, anywhere,” he added. This image shows Eugene assessing discarded footwear he used for his artwork. (Photo: ChannelsTV/Kenny Akinwunmi) The artist shares the detailed process of how he brings each work of art to life. “My process entails getting the materials first, after which we wash them. After we wash them, we have to select and separate them according to their colours, tones, and values.” “I work in two different ways. There’s the assemblage part, where I assemble the footwear. And there’s also the tapestry, where I have to break them into tiny circles and fix them together using copper and aluminium wire,” Eugene explained. Statistics cited by Green Network Asia indicate that over 200 million pairs of flip-flops are discarded each year globally, contributing significantly to plastic and rubber pollution in landfills and oceans. Creating each piece of artwork comes with its challenges, as Eugene says the process can take between two and six months, depending on its size and complexity. “There are a whole lot of challenges that come with the work. There are times when we’re working and have creative blockages. And also, because we work with sharp objects like knives, needles, and all that, there’s also the hazard that comes with it. “I think we work between two to six months, depending on the size and complexity of what we’re working on in the studio,” he said. For Eugene, the message goes beyond the finished artwork, as he hopes his work will change how people perceive and handle discarded materials. “These are materials that are known to be non-biodegradable, meaning all the footwear that I’ve used over the course of the years, they’re all out there. So we are creating awareness through this work so people know what and how to manage their footwear and other fashion waste,” he noted. ‘Reduce, Reuse, Recycle’ Climate change expert Olumide Idowu agrees with Eugene and is calling for more

top.description: The Detroit Lions received some encouraging injury news Wednesday as they prepare for Sunday’s matchup against the New England Patriots in Germany. However, head coach Dan Campbell also revealed that two key starters remain unlikely to play. For now, Wonnum appears to be trending in the right direction, while Mays and Reed face an uphill battle to suit up against the Patriots.

top.title: Bomb threats force evacuation of schools across Italy
top.description: Schools across Italy were evacuated on Wednesday following a series of bomb threats, which Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni described as hoaxes, insisting that there was no concrete danger. The threats, which reportedly affected about 6,000 schools, according to Italian news agency Ansa, citing the Education Ministry, also prompted security concerns in Britain and Ireland, where threatening emails were sent to hundreds of schools. Meloni convened a government meeting with security and intelligence chiefs on Wednesday to review the incidents. Although it was unclear how many Italian schools evacuated their students, crowds of schoolchildren were seen outside educational institutions in different parts of the country. Some students said they had to leave their classrooms hurriedly, abandoning their belongings while awaiting police checks. A 19-year-old student at Rome’s Virgilio High School, Sofia De Ponte, told AFP that the school’s principal announced that a bomb threat had been received by email before ordering an evacuation. “The principal came out into the courtyard and told us that an email had come in, a bomb threat, and right after that the building was evacuated,” she said. De Ponte said the police had yet to arrive because “there’s a long waiting list with all the schools”. “We’re still here waiting,” another student, Elena Sicignano, 19, said. At Brera school in Milan, art teacher Violetta Uboldi said some students appeared delighted by the unexpected break from classes. “I think there was a cry of joy because school was over. That was the reaction,” she said. However, a 16-year-old student, Angelica, said the situation initially caused panic because a teacher had told them it was not a drill. Italian media reported that the threatening email was purportedly signed by a person identified as “Mikhail Andropov, leader of the Vilayat of Misoginistan”. The message claimed that an explosive device had been placed inside a school building and could be detonated remotely. Government Rules Out Immediate Danger The Italian government sought to reassure the public, saying preliminary security checks had not uncovered evidence of an imminent threat. In a Facebook post, Meloni said: “At present, based on the checks carried out, no element has emerged that would suggest there is a concrete danger.” She added that the reports appeared to be part of a strategy designed to cause alarm and concern, adding that investigations were ongoing. Antonello Giannelli, president of the ANP association of Italian school heads, also described the threats as clearly fake. However, he warned that the incident demonstrated how irresponsible actions, amplified by modern communication tools, could cause widespread disruption. “We hope that full light will quickly be shed on the origin of these threats and that those responsible will be identified,” he said. top.title: Skip Bayless says Carson Wentz ‘can’t play football’ after Vikings performance vs Bills
top.description: Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images Carson Wentz’s performance on Monday Night Football drew heavy criticism from everyone in the NFL community, and Skip Bayless joined in by going off on the quarterback. The 33-year-old threw for 81 yards and completed only 8 passes out of 25 attempts, which meant he had a completion rate of only 32%. Wentz ended up with a passer rating of 8.9, which is the lowest for any player with 25 or more passes in the NFL since 2019. His inability to get the ball to the end zone led the Vikings to suffer a 6-23 defeat and pushed them out of the top place in the NFC North. This was Wentz’s chance to prove that he could take over Kyler Murray as the starter, but he put on a horrific performance, which led to the Vikings deciding to trade for Kirk Cousins at the trade deadline, which was just a day after the game. Skip Bayless believes Carson Wentz is not accurate consistently Wentz was a regular starter in the league for 7 seasons. He was a second pick in the 2016 draft by the Philadelphia Eagles; however, he was never able to fulfil the promise he showed at North Dakota State. In the games he has started, Wentz has thrown for over 23,000 yards and completed 62.7% of his passes. But none of that impressed Bayless, who fired shots at Wentz, discussing his performance on Monday Night Football. “I have been hard on him. I was hard on Carson Wentz coming out of college before he got drafted. I didn’t like him at North Dakota State. I didn’t like his poise or his feel. He’s one of those guys who’s the prototype 6’5, 240-pound, rocket-arm quarterback who can’t play football, and he’s not accurate consistently. All he can do is throw it through a brick wall. Well, that’s not how you win NFL games at the highest level,” said Bayless on Gridiron. With Cousins now set to take over the reins as the starting quarterback, Wentz’s future with the Vikings could be questionable. They already have Kyler Murray, who can play as the backup. He is definitely a good piece to have on a team, as he has proven experience starting games, which not a lot of backups in the league have. However, after his performance against the Bills, fans would definitely not be happy if they see him take snaps under center. top.title: Are the Wizards Asking Too Much of Kyshawn George?
top.description: The Washington Wizards have been trying to understand what their young roster can become. Kyshawn George is making a strong case for a big role with the Wizards, but his recent performances have also raised questions about whether the Wizards are putting too much responsibility on him too soon. George has shown that he can help this team in several areas of the game. The 6-foot-7 forward has become a key piece of the Wizards’ offense, using his scoring ability and creative playmaking to make opportunities for himself and his teammates. Over the last few games, George has become particularly encouraging. George scored 22 points against the Orlando Magic on Nov. 2, followed by 25 points facing the Atlanta Hawks on Nov. 4. He then dropped 33 points in another loss to Atlanta the next game, adding eight assists and five three-pointers. Those numbers show why Washington has continued to give George opportunities with the ball in his hands. However, his development isn’t just about scoring and how many points he can score. The Wizards also need to find the right role for him as he continues to improve in the NBA. He’s been able to score, defend multiple positions, and help create offense for his teammates. Washington has also been experimenting with using him as a point guard when Trae Young is not playing. That responsibility has not always been easy. George recorded eight turnovers against the Toronto Raptors on Oct. 23, a performance that showed some of the challenges of asking him to run the Wizards’ offense. He has the ability to make plays, but becoming a good ball handler takes time. After George’s 22-point performance on the Chicago Bulls defense on Oct. 24, Wizards coach Brian Keefe discussed his ability to create more opportunities by getting into the paint. “You saw him being able to create and get into the paint,” Keefe said. “A lot more paint touches for us tonight, which we wanted to emphasize, and he was a catalyst for that.” The comments, reported by Roundtable Sports , show that Washington finds value in what George can bring when he is attacking the basket instead of forcing himself to make all of the plays. The Wizards should continue giving him opportunities to handle the ball, but they should also recognize when he’s most effective. A 19-year-old student at Rome’s Virgilio High School, Sofia De Ponte, told AFP that the school’s principal announced that a bomb threat had been received by email before ordering an evacuation. “The principal came out into the courtyard and told us that an email had come in, a bomb threat, and right after that the building was evacuated,” she said. De Ponte said the police had yet to arrive because “there’s a long waiting list with all the schools”. “We’re still here waiting,” another student, Elena Sicignano, 19, said. That was the reaction,” she said. However, a 16-year-old student, Angelica, said the situation initially caused panic because a teacher had told them it was not a drill. Italian media reported that the threatening email was purportedly signed by a person identified as “Mikhail Andropov, leader of the Vilayat of Misoginistan”. The message claimed that an explosive device had been placed inside a school building and could be detonated remotely. In a Facebook post, Meloni said: “At present, based on the checks carried out, no element has emerged that would suggest there is a concrete danger.” She added that the reports appeared to be part of a strategy designed to cause alarm and concern, adding that investigations were ongoing. Antonello Giannelli, president of the ANP association of Italian school heads, also described the threats as clearly fake. However, he warned that the incident demonstrated how irresponsible actions, amplified by modern communication tools, could cause widespread disruption. “We hope that full light will quickly be shed on the origin of these threats and that those responsible will be identified,” he said. nigeria.title: EU commits €112m to Nigeria’s security, migration management
nigeria.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The European Union (EU) has committed €112 million to support Nigeria’s security operations and migration management efforts as part of measures to strengthen bilateral cooperation between both sides. The EU disclosed this in a statement on Wednesday following the visit of its Commissioner for Internal Affairs and Migration, Mr Magnus Brunner, to Abuja, where he held meetings with key members of the Nigerian government. The funding comprises €66 million for migration-related projects, €26 million for security interventions, including efforts to tackle the proliferation of small arms and drug trafficking, and €20 million under the European Peace Facility to support Nigeria’s counterterrorism efforts. During the visit, Brunner met with the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu; Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Mr Lateef Fagbemi (SAN); Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo; and Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Dr Bernard Doro. The visit came a day after Nigeria and the EU signed the EU-Nigeria Readmission Agreement, aimed at strengthening cooperation on migration management and facilitating the return of Nigerians who do not have the right to remain in EU member states. The EU said its migration partnership with Nigeria had recorded significant improvements in recent years, particularly through cooperation between Nigerian authorities and European agencies, including Europol, Eurojust and Frontex. It added that the partnership had expanded beyond migration to cover security, trade, regional economic cooperation and other areas of mutual interest. According to the statement, bilateral relations gained further momentum following the eighth EU-Nigeria Ministerial Meeting held in Abuja in March, with the participation of the EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, Kaja Kallas. The EU also disclosed that its Global Gateway initiative was being implemented in Nigeria through several projects across different sectors by the EU and its member states under the Team Europe approach. Speaking on the partnership, Brunner said: “Nigeria is a key partner for Europe, and our ties are steadily growing stronger. Together we are turning dialogue into action: more security, better migration management, joining forces to bring results. We are turning the huge potential of our partnership into mutual benefit.” He said the visit provided an opportunity to review the partnership, advance cooperation on shared priorities and prepare for further engagement between both sides in areas beyond migration and security. nigeria.title: Nigeria crude oil production hits 1.68mbpd – NUPRC
nigeria.description: Nigeria produced an average of 1.687 million barrels of crude oil and condensate per day in October 2026, the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) has said. Data released by the commission on Wednesday showed that daily production peaked at 1.79 million barrels per day (bpd), while the lowest output during the month was 1.60 million bpd. The data showed that crude oil production, excluding condensate, averaged 1.51 million barrels per day (mbpd) during the review period. This represented 101 per cent of Nigeria’s 1.5 million bpd production quota allocated by the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC). According to the report, Nigeria had met its assigned OPEC crude oil production quota for six consecutive months. It said the country produced 1.53 million bpd in May, 1.55 million bpd in June, 1.51 million bpd in July, 1.50 million bpd in August, 1.53 million bpd in September and 1.51 million bpd in October. The report, however, indicated a 1.7 per cent month-on-month decline in crude oil production. It attributed the relatively stable performance in recent months to improved operational stability, production uptime and crude evacuation efficiency. The commission said the sustained performance in October reflected the commitment of operators and industry stakeholders to improving operational efficiency, maintaining asset integrity and enhancing production reliability across the upstream sector. A breakdown of daily average crude oil and condensate production by terminals and streams showed that Forcados Terminal recorded the highest output of 318.49 thousand barrels per day (kbpd). Bonny Terminal followed with 311.02 kbpd, while Qua Iboe Terminal recorded 173.97 kbpd. This is one of the biggest milestones in my career.” For all Kane’s brilliance, England have not won a major men’s international trophy since lifting the 1966 World Cup on home soil. For large brands, the real question is not simply how to find more influencers. Brands need repeatable ways to identify creators, review content, approve campaigns, manage payments, protect the brand, measure results, and learn from previous activity. The goal is to move from individual creator activations to a repeatable marketing channel. Large organizations may have global marketing teams, regional managers, product divisions, legal departments, procurement teams, local agencies, and paid media specialists involved in the same campaign. nigeria.title: CAC, EY warn directors against governance failures
nigeria.description: By Peter Egwuatu The Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) has warned company directors against treating regulatory compliance as the sole responsibility of company secretaries, saying weak corporate records and governance failures could undermine business credibility, investment prospects and access to credit. The Registrar-General and Chief Executive Officer of CAC, Hussaini Ishaq Magaji, gave the warning at the 2026 Audit Committee Transformation Summit organised by Ernst & Young (EY) in Lagos on Wednesday. Magaji said directors’ responsibilities extended beyond strategy, profitability and risk management to protecting the integrity of their companies’ legal identities. He noted that outdated corporate records, undisclosed changes in ownership and failure to file annual returns could expose companies to regulatory sanctions, reputational damage and diminished investor confidence. According to him, “Directors must demonstrate diligence, transparency and accountability by ensuring accurate corporate records, timely statutory filings and proper disclosure of persons with significant control. “The era of filing annual returns as an annual ritual is over. The Corporate Affairs Commission is asking Nigerian boards and companies to move beyond merely filing annual returns towards continuous accountability, transparent ownership, accurate records and credible governance.” He added that companies with transparent ownership structures and disciplined governance would be better positioned to attract investments, secure credit, participate in public procurement and pursue business partnerships. The ordinance, which amends the Bank of Russia’s rules for organized trading, was registered by the Justice Ministry on Nov. 3 and published Wednesday on the regulator’s site. It takes effect 10 days after publication, on Nov. 22. Exchanges will have to register the brokers, trust managers and central counterparties that take part in crypto trades, keep registers of orders and deals, and monitor the activity. They must also calculate a current price, a weighted-average price, a market price and a closing price, and report trading activity to the central bank in the same way they already do for other assets. The regulator was clear about the order of operations. Exchanges may open crypto markets from Nov. 22, it said, “but first they must agree with the regulator on the rules for conducting such trading.” It did not say whether any venue has already cleared that review. The Bank of Russia approved bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT for purchase by non-qualified investors, and said exchanges may admit those assets to public trading from that date. Non-qualified investors can buy through a broker, a trust manager or a registered crypto exchange office, on an exchange or over the counter. Purchases through a single intermediary may not exceed 300,000 rubles a year, roughly $3,600 at the official exchange rate. Qualified investors can access all cryptoassets with no purchase cap. Both groups still have to pass a knowledge test and read a risk disclosure before they can trade. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine ICE and OKX Set Nov. 23 Tokenized Stock Launch After 67 Companies Opt Out OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) will open their tokenized stock venue on Nov. 23, the companies said Wednesday, offering more than 70 assets under a temporary SEC exemption even as 67 companies, including Apple, Tesla and Meta, have already objected. The OKX announcement said more than 70 assets are expected to be listed, including securities from Better.com, BitGo, Circle, Coinbase, Robinhood, Securitize and Strategy (MSTR), as well as 59 exchange-traded funds from Direxion. The bank announced the service on Sept. 16, saying it would go live with first clients this year once regulators signed off. It now supports bitcoin and ether, along with the USDC, EURC and EURAU stablecoins, according to its product page . Under the setup, Deutsche Bank manages the wallets and private keys on behalf of clients, who can store the assets and transfer them to third parties. The bank pitched that as a way for clients to skip building and maintaining their own custody infrastructure. “In the medium term we aim to deliver a fully integrated, regulated ecosystem that supports the custody, tokenisation, and settlement of digital assets,” said Paul Maley, global head of trust and securities services at Deutsche Bank. The bank did not name its first clients, say how many have signed up or disclose what it charges to hold the coins. The service is aimed at institutional and corporate clients, not retail customers. Clients reach the service through Autobahn, Deutsche Bank’s multi-channel gateway, or its Corporate Bank portal. The service is booked out of Deutsche Bank AG in Frankfurt and is available in Germany, with cross-border servicing across Europe through passporting. The bank lists institutional investors, multinationals and corporates, governments and sovereigns, and wealth managers as target clients, and it describes the offering as compliant with the European Union’s MiCA crypto rules. For now the menu is narrow. Deutsche lists custody, transfers and internal moves between warm and cold storage as its initial services, with “further capabilities planned.” The September release said the asset list may grow with client demand and that tokenized financial instruments are on the roadmap. It also carried a warning familiar to anyone in bitcoin: crypto assets held this way are not covered by a deposit-guarantee scheme like the one that protects eligible bank deposits. entertainment.title: What Are The Effective Ways of Using AI?
entertainment.description: Two people engaging with technology in a contemporary hotel lobby work setting. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing how people learn, work, communicate and solve problems. In today’s world, if you’re not on board with AI, it could be said you’re being resistant to the fastest-growing technological innovation in the world. From students researching academic subjects to professionals developing business ideas, AI tools have become companions in everyday activities for people. They can help save time, explore new ideas, understand difficult concepts and approach tasks differently. However, as more people embrace these AI tools, it is important to understand that using AI effectively goes beyond knowing what prompts to enter. It requires knowing when to use it, how to question its responses and, most importantly, when to rely on your own knowledge and judgement. AI could make us better at what we do, not make us dependent on it. Here are ways we think you use AI effectively: Use AI as a Research Assistant One of the most effective ways to use AI is for research and information gathering. Whether you are writing an article, preparing a presentation or exploring an unfamiliar subject, AI can help you identify relevant topics, explain complex ideas and suggest areas worth investigating. You can ask it to break down unfamiliar concepts, identify key questions, or suggest research directions. However, do not treat every response as fact. Verify important information using credible sources, published research, books and reliable websites. AI can help you find information, but you are responsible for establishing what is true. Use AI to Brainstorm and Explore Ideas Like knowledge gathering, AI can brainstorm ideas with you. Sometimes, the hardest part of starting a project is knowing where to begin. AI can help you overcome this challenge by suggesting ideas, exploring different approaches and presenting perspectives you may not have considered. For writers, entrepreneurs, researchers and creatives, it can be a useful brainstorming partner. You can share an idea, ask questions about its strengths and weaknesses, and explore ways to develop it. However, brainstorming should not become an excuse to surrender your imagination. Let AI expand your thinking, not replace it. Use AI to Improve Your Work, Not Replace Your Skills This is becoming more important. AI can help you identify grammatical errors, improve sentence construction, organise information, summarise lengthy documents and make your communication clearer. It can reduce the time spent on repetitive tasks and create more room for important responsibilities. The important thing is that you should remain actively involved. Photo Credit: Skepta/Instagram Your playlist could do with a little shake-up, and these five albums might be exactly what it needs. Skepta is reconnecting with his roots, Phyno is giving us more of the indigenous rap we love, Ty Bello has two albums exploring different expressions of worship, and Anendlessocean and Tobe Nwigwe are taking their sounds in interesting directions. From UK grime and Nigerian hip-hop to alternative gospel and soul, there’s a lot to discover across these new releases. Whether you’re in the mood for bars, worship, thoughtful songwriting or music that brings different cultures together, this week’s selection has something worth hearing. Skepta: The Fork & Knife Back in 2012, Skepta found himself at odds with a corporatised grime scene, sparking a pivotal career reckoning that eventually led to his landmark 2016 album Konnichiwa. On his long-awaited 15-track sixth album, The Fork & Knife, the 44-year-old MC reflects on his journey as grime’s most influential elder statesman and the son of Nigerian immigrants. Named after his mother’s favourite proverb, the record is a deep exploration of identity and perseverance. Musically, Skepta bridges continents by blending global diasporic sounds. He teams up with Aya Nakamura on the zouk-infused “ Chippie ”, taps Asake for the Afrobeats crossover “ Aloe Vera ”, and recruits Chase & Status alongside Suggs for the sharp single “ Innocent Smile ”. The project closes with “ Belly ”, an eight-minute masterclass featuring Boy Better Know members Jme and Frisco . ﻿ Phyno: Let That Sink In Arriving nearly 10 years after his groundbreaking sophomore record The Playmaker, Phyno’s 15-track sixth solo album, Let That Sink In (LTSI), showcases his timeless command of indigenous rap. Across the record,the Enugu-born star blends soul, R&B, and traditional Nigerian sounds to explore faith, resilience, and personal evolution. The album features powerhouse collaborations, including Seyi Vibez on the opener “ Ndu Ka Aku ”, Fireboy DML on “ I Believe ”, and Jeriq on “ Ije Enu ”. Whether taking the government to task on “20 Years to Come” or offering uplifting anthems like “ Chukwu Okike ”, Phyno proves why he remains a definitive voice in African hip-hop. ﻿ Ty Bello: I Speak Lion and I Speak Lamb Creative powerhouse Ty Bello delivers a massive double-album listening experience with I Speak Lion and I Speak Lamb . Split into two distinct spiritual volumes, the expansive project captures both the bold, triumphant authority of worship and its quiet, intimate moments. ﻿ I Speak Lion leans into explosive, high-energy sounds designed to spark courage, featuring powerful pairings with Sunmisola Agbebi , Greatman Takit , and Limoblaze . Presented on 27 October 2026 at The Sphere, Lagos, the collection draws from the familiar expression to stand on ceremony: to insist on the observance of formalities. For Ifeyinwa Azubike, the idea presents an opportunity to examine the traditions women inherit, the rituals they observe and the choices they make when dressing for themselves. The collection is built around two identities: The Devotee and The Rebel. They are not opposing personalities so much as two ways of relating to ceremony. The Devotee embraces its rituals. She understands the language of formal dressing and participates in it with intention. For her, dressing fully is an expression of desire and personal conviction. The Rebel is equally familiar with the rules, but she is selective about the ones she follows. Her approach to dressing allows for disruption, though never simply for the sake of attention. Through these characters, Azubike considers a familiar experience for women: the pull between what an occasion expects and what an individual wants to express. Speaking on the theme “Losing the Fear” , at The International Women Leadership Conference (TIWLC) in Dubai, organised by the Ibukun Awosika Leadership Foundation, Ekeh , who was a keynote speaker on the final day of this year’s conference, addressed over 600 women industry leaders from different countries across the globe. sports.title: Skip Bayless says Carson Wentz ‘can’t play football’ after Vikings performance vs Bills
sports.description: Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images Carson Wentz’s performance on Monday Night Football drew heavy criticism from everyone in the NFL community, and Skip Bayless joined in by going off on the quarterback. The 33-year-old threw for 81 yards and completed only 8 passes out of 25 attempts, which meant he had a completion rate of only 32%. Wentz ended up with a passer rating of 8.9, which is the lowest for any player with 25 or more passes in the NFL since 2019. His inability to get the ball to the end zone led the Vikings to suffer a 6-23 defeat and pushed them out of the top place in the NFC North. This was Wentz’s chance to prove that he could take over Kyler Murray as the starter, but he put on a horrific performance, which led to the Vikings deciding to trade for Kirk Cousins at the trade deadline, which was just a day after the game. Skip Bayless believes Carson Wentz is not accurate consistently Wentz was a regular starter in the league for 7 seasons. He was a second pick in the 2016 draft by the Philadelphia Eagles; however, he was never able to fulfil the promise he showed at North Dakota State. In the games he has started, Wentz has thrown for over 23,000 yards and completed 62.7% of his passes. But none of that impressed Bayless, who fired shots at Wentz, discussing his performance on Monday Night Football. “I have been hard on him. I was hard on Carson Wentz coming out of college before he got drafted. I didn’t like him at North Dakota State. I didn’t like his poise or his feel. He’s one of those guys who’s the prototype 6’5, 240-pound, rocket-arm quarterback who can’t play football, and he’s not accurate consistently. All he can do is throw it through a brick wall. Well, that’s not how you win NFL games at the highest level,” said Bayless on Gridiron. With Cousins now set to take over the reins as the starting quarterback, Wentz’s future with the Vikings could be questionable. They already have Kyler Murray, who can play as the backup. He is definitely a good piece to have on a team, as he has proven experience starting games, which not a lot of backups in the league have. However, after his performance against the Bills, fans would definitely not be happy if they see him take snaps under center. But there’s plenty of reason for optimism, as Houston is tied for the top odds at 32.9% to land the No. 1 overall pick. For her, she wants someone like A’ja Wilson , who brings an unmatched work ethic and leadership that can reshape an entire franchise from day one. “You know, obviously, you know, when you look at like who’s done it the best, you’ve got to look at A’ja Wilson, right? So she wanted to not just be the best coming out of college, but she wanted to be the best period. And then you add on top of it her leadership, right? Beyond the numbers, her relentless drive and locker-room leadership are why she’s the absolute gold standard for what a WNBA superstar looks like today. sports.title: Barcelona prioritise January move for €20 million-rated teenage defender – report
sports.description: Barcelona prioritise January move for €20 million-rated teenage defender – report According to Ferran Correas of SPORT , Barcelona have decided to go after the signing of FC Twente defender Ruud Nijstad in the upcoming January transfer window as a priority. Director Deco and the Barcelona sporting department want to strengthen Hansi Flick’s defensive options, and the 18-year-old Dutchman remains high on their list despite the financial obstacles involved. Barcelona want a new defender Barcelona opted not to sign a new central defender in the summer despite letting go of Ronald Araujo and Alvaro Cortes. However, the injuries to Andreas Christensen, Eric Garcia, and Jules Kounde exposed the lack of depth in the position, leaving Flick short on options. Even though Christensen is back, Barcelona’s position on signing a reinforcement has not changed, as the club continue to see Garcia and Kounde as primarily options in the right-back position. Barcelona ready to go after Nijstad again. (Photo by Mateo Villalba Sanchez/Getty Images for DFB) It leaves the manager with only Pau Cubarsi, Gerard Martin and an injury-prone Christensen as main options at the heart of the backline. As such, Barcelona have made the decision to go after a new centre-back in January, with the preference being to sign someone with a long-term view rather than a stop-gap fix for only the second half of the season. Nijstad emerges as the preferred option And, even though there have been links to several players such as Natan of Real Betis and Manchester United star Lisandro Martinez, Nijstad has emerged as the priority target for Barcelona . The Blaugrana made contact to explore a move for the defender last summer, but nothing materialised as Nijstad, who also attracted interest from other major European clubs, opted to stay at Twente. The 18-year-old defender has a contract with the Dutch club running until June 2029, and his performances have pushed his valuation upwards. Deco does not want to spend €20 million on Nijstad. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) As such, Twente are looking for a transfer fee of around €20 million for the teenage centre-back, a figure Barcelona are unwilling to meet. The Blaugrana appreciate the youngster’s profile and value his immense potential, but see the transfer fee being quoted as higher than what they intend to spend. Moreover, there is also the difficulty of Financial Fair Play, as the Catalans only have a margin of around €3-4 million. While that may have improved following Raphinha’s renewal, it still restricts the club’s spending power. As such, the future of Alejandro Balde, who is linked with a January exit, could play a key role in Barcelona’s pursuit of Nijstad.

technology.title: Scientists check their work and confirm it with update on iconic black hole image
technology.description: The image of the red ring around the black hole M87, produced by the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) array, made front-page news around the world in 2019. There was one problem: there was a slim chance the depiction might be wrong. This week, a small team of four Australian researchers have published their work confirming the result based on a new machine learning algorithm using the same base data. The 2019 Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) image came from hundreds of scientists working together to capture the first direct view of a black hole's shadow. The measurements were taken at eight telescopes around the world, at locations including Chile, the US, and Antarctica. Reconstructing the image from the data so geographically distant meant instrument and environment errors could influence the accuracy of the resulting image. Potentially, alternative analyses of the data could have reconstructed an image without the iconic ring shape. Samuel Lai – a postdoctoral fellow at the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO) in Western Australia – and his team created an independent imaging algorithm to process the historic dataset to validate the result. The new approach used closed triplets (using three telescopes for error correction) rather than station pairs in an effort to reduce error. To the relief of the EHT team, the new image recreated the iconic ring-like image seen in the original, according to a paper published in Nature today . In a prepared statement, Lai said taking pictures of black holes was not easy. "It is like standing in your backyard and trying to take a photo of a doughnut on the Moon," he said. He explained that when his team applied new advanced machine learning and artificial intelligence techniques to the original Event Horizon Telescope dataset, they found a black hole almost identical in size and shape to the historic EHT image. "Importantly, our model had no idea what a black hole looked like when we applied it to the M87 data. This is the first truly independent validation of the EHT image, an important step in the scientific process," he said. Event Horizon Telescope director Laurent Loinard welcomed the new study. "It is extremely gratifying to see that an elegant, entirely independent method recovers the ring structure of M87 across several years, in excellent agreement with the EHT Collaboration's published results," he said. ®

technology.description: Apple's first touchscreen MacBook got a mixed reception from iFixit's teardown specialists, who praised its easily replaced lid but found fans and USB-C ports buried beneath the logic board. The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display was unveiled at the end of October. It features a tandem OLED screen that stacks two layers of organic light-emitting pixels, eliminating the need for a backlight, and adds touch capability to the MacBook line for the first time. Although the vendor was patted on the back in recent years for improving the repairability of its famously locked-down products, this machine shows Apple still has some way to go. The good? The entire lid comes off relatively easily. Its three-screw hinges closely resemble those on the M6 14-inch MacBook Pro, while streamlined display cable brackets simplify removal. Apple's Repair Assistant tool also handled a full system board swap well. Despite concerns about Touch ID fingerprint authentication, everything went relatively smoothly when iFixit paired a touchscreen from one machine with a logic board from another. On the first boot, Repair Assistant recognized the battery, display, and Touch ID sensor, and touch control needed no separate calibration. The bad? Replacing the panel alone is not possible. When iFixit tried to separate it from the lid, the glass delaminated, cracking the OLED and touch-sensitive layers beneath. That could make for a costlier repair than bargained for. Under the bottom cover, the PROLED has a similar internal layout to the last few models of MacBook Pros, with the fans, board, speakers, and trackpad all in the same places. That means the same annoyances persist. The MagSafe power connector can be removed via two screws and a bracket, yet the USB-C ports can't be extracted the same way because the logic board is in the way. The headphone jack and the fans also require removing the system board first, and the HDMI port and SDXC card reader are soldered to the board itself, as is the storage and memory. Another gripe is that this MacBook's battery pack is hard to remove, though at least it is removable, unlike in many thin-and-light laptops. The tested Pro weighs 1.38 kg or about 3 pounds. For these reasons, the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display earns a 5 out of 10 repairability score from iFixit , but this is actually a one point increase over the score it gave the M5 MacBook Pro. In the hours after the patch was released, multiple complaints began to surface that the download and installation were failing, with some customers reporting a 0x800F0993 error code. Others say they received a 0x800F0989 error. Microsoft does not currently list any known issues with the update and is yet to make a statement or provide explanation for the glitch. In addition to the security fixes, this patch resolves a number of known issues from previous updates, including a problem where USB Audio 1.0 devices might fail to start and display an error code 10 in Device Manager. In the absence of a statement from Microsoft, several users have taken to sleuthing. One, with the handle of Forceflow on the ElevenForum site, suggested the bug might be related to Windows Sandbox, and said that after disabling the feature and rebooting, the patch installed successfully. However, others reported problems regardless of Windows Sandbox status, and alternative solutions included using DISM (Deployment Image Servicing and Management) to check the package or downloading the update manually. It's an important patch to install, since it addresses 726 vulnerabilities in Windows alone, and the difficulties affected users face are less than ideal. Microsoft patches have lately displayed more gremlins than usual. Out-of-band releases are depressingly regular after updates break functionality. A September Out-of-band release, for example, was hurriedly pushed out after the September 2026 Windows security update caused trouble for Remote Desktop Services. The October Patch Tuesday for Windows Server sent Exchange Servers toppling , with a registry edit workaround suggested. There was no out-of-band update - Microsoft said the problem had been resolved in the November update. At least this latest release appears to be failing before users get a chance to see what is broken this time. The Register has asked Microsoft to comment. ®

technology.title: NASA asks Earthlings to wave as Voyager 1 reaches a light-day away
technology.description: Voyager 1 will become the first human-made object to reach one light-day from Earth next week, and NASA wants us to mark the occasion by flashing our lights at the sky. The spacecraft, which suffered a communications hiccup last month, is traveling at approximately 38,000 mph (61,000 kph) and will mark the 50th anniversary of its launch next year. Before then, it has another distance record to set. "Light-day" is a bit snappier than 16,094,799,096 miles (25,902,068,356 kilometers). NASA puts the crossing at 05:16:07 EST (10:16:07 UTC) on Wednesday, November 18. For "Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day," participants are invited to flash the mission's three-letter designation – VGR – in Morse code after sunset on November 17, using a flashlight or NASA's website. According to the space agency, this will create "a symbolic wave of golden light encircling the planet after sunset." It is also a nice way to mark the achievement – Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object from Earth, and its extraordinary longevity remains a testament to the skill of engineers past and present. Not that Voyager 1 will be able to detect any flashlights on Earth. Its cameras were turned off decades ago, after the famous Pale Blue Dot image was captured. NASA has invited the public to join in a spacecraft photo opportunity before. On July 19, 2013, Cassini photographed Earth and the Moon from its orbit around Saturn for "The Day the Earth Smiled," while people back home were encouraged to look up and "just smile at the sheer joy of being alive on a Pale Blue Dot." Voyager 2, the spacecraft's sibling, is not expected to reach the same milestone for another nine years. It took a different path through the solar system to swing past Uranus and Neptune. It will, however, be uncertain as to whether Voyager 2 will still be able to communicate by then – even with recent efforts to eke out the probe's dwindling power supply, margins are razor thin. ®

It serves as further independent validation of the cryptography that protects massive quantities of the world's communications on platforms like the Signal app , Google Messages, and WhatsApp. And it demonstrates Google DeepMind's formal verification capabilities using a new AI framework called AlphaProof Code. More broadly, AI-aided formal verification is having a moment, but it is unclear how practical it will be for widespread use and how effective it can be at securing large amounts of code. Proponents of formal verification have long referred to it as a sort of holy grail in software security, because it uses math to check and validate that software is functioning as intended—in other words, that it doesn't have critical vulnerabilities. science.title: Who will step up to preserve space age artefacts for future generations?
science.description: NASA/JPL-Caltech Around 40,000 years from now, the Voyager 1 probe will pass within astronomical spitting distance of the star Gliese 445. From there, it will continue drifting through the universe on an endless journey that marks humanity’s first attempt to reach the stars. Voyager 1 – which on 18 November will have travelled one light day from Earth – began its odyssey almost 50 years ago, meaning it has been operating for the majority of the space age. That makes it a rarity: most of our iconic spacecraft ended their lives burned up in Earth’s atmosphere or in bits at the bottom of the ocean. Two of the most important missions still flying today, the Hubble Space Telescope and the International Space Station, look set to share the same fate in the near future, even as scientists call for Hubble to be preserved . While some craft like the space shuttles are on display in museums, our present space history is, essentially, in its dark ages, with little thought currently given to preserving spacecraft in situ, where our space-travelling descendants may wish to marvel at them. Even the Apollo hardware left behind on the moon has almost no protection in international law. Advertisement Perhaps we need an organisation like the UNESCO World Heritage Committee to designate important space artefacts for preservation, and encourage funding from cultural and heritage budgets, not scientific ones, to do this. Of course, with such budgets often under threat and the US set to leave UNESCO at the end of this year, this could introduce new problems. Private philanthropy is another option. If humanity is to one day take its place among the stars, a fantasy that fuels many a tech billionaire, it would be a great shame to not be able to look back at how we got there. Just as we remember 19th-century captains of industry like Andrew Carnegie and J. P. Morgan for funding great cultural institutions, perhaps we should be lobbying for the creation of a Musk Space Museum or Bezos Orbital Institute.

science.description: Josie Ford Feedback is our weekly column of bizarre stories, implausible advertising claims, confusing instructions and more Caught on camera One of the defining features of conspiracy theories is that they are “self-sealing”. If you confront a conspiracy theorist with the lack of evidence for their claim, they will turn this back on you and argue that this very lack of evidence is proof of how powerful the conspiracy is. This is foreshadowing. Advertisement Feedback is interested in watching the new documentary Capturing Bigfoot . We can’t, because we live in the UK and it isn’t available here , but if anyone would care to rectify that, we will stick ourselves in front of it immediately. The film is about the classic footage that purports to show a Bigfoot loping alongside a river in California. Shot by Roger Patterson and Robert Gimlin in 1967, the clip became one of the canonical pieces of evidence for the existence of Bigfoot: a mythical humanoid that supposedly lives in the forests of North America. Bigfoot is one of the icons of cryptozoology, the search for probably-nonexistent creatures. It has hordes of devotees. In Capturing Bigfoot , film-maker Marq Evans uncovers what really happened in 1967. He speaks to Patterson’s associate Bob Heironimus, who says he wore an ape costume in the footage. Crucially, Evans also finds a lost piece of 16-millimetre film, shot in 1966, showing a rehearsal for the final Patterson-Gimlin video. A review of the documentary in Variety calls this footage “the smoking gun”. It is, Feedback would suggest, a case no defence lawyer could wriggle out of. So, the Patterson-Gimlin film purporting to show Bigfoot was fake. Feedback and our editor worried if we were legally safe saying that, but then, as our editor said, “come on”. It is perhaps telling that, when we mentioned this to Mrs Feedback, her response was “I could have sworn I already knew that”. science.title: Extraordinary image of bioluminescent plankton captured by photographer
science.description: Lucifer’s Vortex by Tom Fecht Tom Fecht On the edge of twilight, the surface of the sea glows. Millions of tiny dots produce an eerie blue light, barely visible to humans. Each one is a single plankton shining with bioluminescence, and the dots’ light blurs together as the waters churn around them. Tom Fecht captured this image in Brittany, France, looking down into the Atlantic Ocean under a bright moon. The luminescence of the plankton is dim, so his first attempts to catch it resulted in nothing but darkness. “I figured something must be going on which you couldn’t see with the naked eye, so I just blindly started opening the shutter every time a wave broke,” says Fecht. Finally, he captured the light from the plankton mixing with reflections of moonlight in a churning wave. He titled the image Lucifer’s Vortex after the compounds, called luciferins, that generate this light. While these plankton aren’t officially endangered – no plankton species is, in part due to the impossibility of tracking them individually – their future is highly uncertain. Warmer waters force them to migrate polewards and, in some places, die off, their access to nutrients blocked by changing ocean currents. Advertisement The word “luciferin” comes from the Latin for “light-bringer”, and Fecht hopes the plankton’s otherworldly glow also brings light to the plight they face. “If you want to engage in protecting nature, you first of all need an understanding of its beauty,” he says. science.title: Did comets bring building blocks of life to Earth? Scientists aren't so sure anymore
science.description: The origin of life on Earth remains a mystery. New research shows that comets almost certainly did not bring the chemical building blocks of life to our planet. Life as we know it is based around carbon chemistry, also known as organic chemistry. Complex organic molecules are the fundamental building blocks of biochemical compounds such as nucleobases, amino acids, sugars and so on that act as the machinery for biochemistry on Earth . Two big questions are where did this complex chemistry originate? Did these complex organic molecules form on Earth, or were they delivered here from space? New research led by planetary scientist Richard Anslow of the Institute for Astronomy at the University of Cambridge has now seemingly ruled out comets as the origin of complex organic molecules on Earth. "Historically, scientists thought that comets were important for the origin of life on Earth, because they carried carbon and nitrogen-bearing molecules, so these giant space snowballs were almost like a 'get-out-of-jail-free card' that brought all the molecules a planet would need to seed life," said Anslow in a statement . Stripping the romance from the Earth's turbulent past Comet impacts on Earth were much more frequent in the first half-billion years of the solar system ’s existence, when there were still lots of debris leftover from the formation of the planets. For over a century comet impacts had been considered a prime suspect in the search for what brought the building blocks of life to Earth. However, while comets bringing the building blocks of life to Earth is "kind of a romantic idea," according to Anslow, the University of Cambridge researcher added that the team's results suggest that is highly unlikely. Anslow and colleagues arrived at this conclusion based upon computer modeling by using the very latest simulations depicting the origin and evolution of comets and their orbits, their interactions with Earth's atmosphere as they enter it, and of the hypervelocity comet impacts themselves. In particular, they used the fate of hydrogen cyanide as a proxy for what happens to complex organic molecules in comet impacts. Hydrogen cyanide is frequently found in comets and was even detected in the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS . An artist’s impression of a comet crashing into the early Earth (Image credit: Scarlett White) The problem is that comets are generally moving at too great a velocity. For organic molecules to survive impact, the impact velocity would have to be below 33,500 miles per hour (15 kilometers per second). Anslow and his colleagues found that, in general, comets travel too fast and enter Earth’s atmosphere at too sharp an angle for complex organic molecules to survive. Instead, they are mostly vaporized on impact. Even on the rare occasions that the complex organic molecules survived, they were usually not in great enough abundance to provide any meaningful prebiotic chemistry. science.title: 'There's tremendous demand': Rocket Lab raises price of Neutron launch from $55 million to $70 million
science.description: null The coming launch bottleneck has ramped up demand for a rocket that has yet to leave the ground. Rocket Lab announced on Monday (Nov. 9) that it recently raised the price of a Neutron launch from $55 million to $70 million — an increase of more than 25%, for a ride on a rocket that's set to debut in 2027. "Launch is extremely constrained, and that is exactly the situation we predicted," Rocket Lab founder and CEO Peter Beck said on Monday during the company's third-quarter earnings call. "We saw a pent-up launch market on the horizon, and rather than provide early discounted launches, we set out to deliver a rocket into an environment with extreme demand at full price or higher." Rocket Lab is best known for Electron , a workhorse small-satellite launcher that debuted in 2017 and now has 90 orbital missions under its belt. The 59-foot-tall (18 meters) expendable rocket and can haul 660 pounds (300 kilograms) to low Earth orbit (LEO). Neutron is the company's entry into the medium-lift market. It features a reusable first stage, stands 141 feet (43 m) tall and can carry 14.3 tons (13 metric tons) of payload to LEO. Rocket Lab announced Neutron back in 2021 and first targeted a 2024 debut for the vehicle. But various problems have cropped up over the years, pushing things back. Last month, for example, Rocket Lab announced that it was delaying the first Neutron flight from late 2026 into 2027 due to a manufacturing issue (which it says is now under control). Such setbacks have not dampened demand for Neutron's services, however. During Monday's call, Beck revealed that Rocket Lab booked eight Neutron launches during the third quarter of 2026, which ran from July 1 through Sept. 30. The contracts for those eight flights are worth "a total of roughly 515 million, including multiple missions on a new escalated base price of $70 million," Beck said. Neutron's first 16 launches are now sold out, he added, and bookings from here on will be for flights in the 2030s. "The demand is a function of both a tightening global launch supply and our customers' confidence that Rocket Lab is the right partner to break the world's launch bottleneck," Beck said. science.title: Hubble Space Telescope reveals glittering stars with mysterious origins | Space photo of the day for Nov. 11, 2026
science.description: null The Hubble Space Telescope has captured a breathtaking view of thousands of stars glittering like cosmic jewels in a dazzling display of blue, gold and orange. But this spectacular scene is far more than just a pretty picture. Some of these stars are almost as old as the universe itself and could hold clues to how our Milky Way formed. M30 is a globular star cluster located approximately 27,500 light-years from Earth. (Image credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA, M. Libralato, G. Piotto, A. Sarajedini) What is it? The exquisite image released by ESA on Nov. 5 shows Messier 30 (M30), a densely packed collection of stars located approximately 27,500 light-years from Earth in the constellation Capricornus. M30 is a globular cluster, a roughly spherical collection of tens of thousands to millions of stars held together by gravity . Our Milky Way is home to at least 150 of these ancient stellar gatherings, some of which are estimated to be between 11.5 billion and 13.5 billion years old. For comparison, the universe itself is approximately 13.8 billion years old! Why is it amazing Besides looking like a vast cosmic treasure trove glittering across the universe, M30 also has a fascinating story to tell. Globular clusters are essentially cosmic time capsules. Their ancient stars preserve chemical clues about the conditions that existed when they formed, helping astronomers piece together the Milky Way's early history. Astronomers have also discovered that M30, along with several other globular clusters, traverses the Milky Way in the opposite direction to the galaxy's rotation. This unusual motion raises the intriguing possibility that M30 may not have formed in our galaxy at all. It could have simply been captured by the Milky Way billions of years ago.

science.title: NASA's new UVEX space telescope will peer deep into the universe's most violent events
science.description: null A new NASA space telescope will study the universe in ultraviolet light to reveal the violent and turbulent events that bubble under what appears to be a cosmic sea of tranquility. The Ultraviolet Explorer (UVEX) mission, developed by NASA in conjunction with the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), will be the first mission to create deep all-sky maps in ultraviolet light. Thus, when it launches in 2031, UVEX will join new sky-mapping surveys like NASA's SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer), which scans the cosmos in infrared, and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, which does the same over the southern hemisphere in visible light, in creating deep-sky maps across a broad swathe of the electromagnetic spectrum. UVEX's ultraviolet views will reveal explosive events such as the collisions between ultra-dense stellar corpses called neutron stars and the supernova explosions that mark the deaths of massive stars and the births of neutron stars and black holes. Additionally, the NASA ultraviolet telescope should be able to detect a multitude of low-mass galaxies much closer to the Milky Way than similar galaxies that are currently being observed millions and even billions of light-years away by NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) . The $590 million UVEX mission will "advance fundamental frontiers in astrophysics, from understanding the smallest galaxies to diagnosing the aftermath of neutron-star mergers and other cosmic explosions," the mission's principal investigator, Caltech physics professor Fiona Harrison, said in an Oct. 27 statement . "The first major ultraviolet space mission in two decades, UVEX is a bold leap forward in our exploration of the ultraviolet universe," Caltech President Ray Jayawardhana said in the same statement. UVEX will paint a picture of cosmic life, death and afterlife UVEX will benefit from a major leap forward in UV sensitivity thanks to its Caltech-built sensors, which are based on complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) imaging technology. This will help the spacecraft tap into what Harrison described as "the untapped opportunity in the UV." UVEX will be uniquely poised to spot millions of nearby, small, and faint galaxies that are teeming with infant stars that emit bright UV light. "In optical light, it's very hard to distinguish these nearby galaxies from faraway ones that look similar," Harrison said. "UV light will make them easier to find." UVEX won't just be investigating the infancy of stars , however. It will also examine the deaths of ancient stars in the form of supernovas. science.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 11 – NGC… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. NGC 4449: Small Galaxy, Big Impact Explanation: Don’t judge a galaxy by its size. Our home galaxy, the Milky Way , is about 100,000 light years across. This huge expanse of space contains hundreds of billions of stars! The smallest galaxies, called dwarf galaxies , are about 1/10th the size of the Milky Way and only contain a few billion stars. They are also the most common type of galaxy in the whole universe. Today’s image shows one such dwarf galaxy, NGC 4449 , captured by the Hubble Space Telescope . NGC 4449 and similar dwarf galaxies are missing more oxygen than models predict. This suggests their stellar winds and supernovae are surprisingly effective at blowing away oxygen and other heavy elements. Turns out these tiny galaxies may play a big role in spreading heavy elements — the building blocks of stars, planets, and life — throughout the universe! science.title: SpaceX moves Starship Flight 15 booster to launch pad for 'squeeze test' ahead of epic double-catch attempt (photos)
science.description: null SpaceX is one big step closer to the 15th test flight of its Starship megarocket. The company announced today (Nov. 10) that it had moved its latest Starship first stage, known as Super Heavy Booster 22, to the launch mount at its Starbase facility in South Texas ahead of Flight 15, which is scheduled to lift off this Friday (Nov. 13). During the upcoming launch test, SpaceX plans to catch both Booster 22 and Starship's Ship upper stage with its launch tower's "chopstick" arms in a double landing catch — something the private spaceflight company has never tried before. It will be the first full recovery of an orbital rocket in history. SpaceX's Flight 15 Starship Super Heavy booster in its assembly bay, before its move to Starbase's launch mount. (Image credit: SpaceX) Booster 22 therefore "was used for final catch testing upon arrival [at the pad], including a suspended squeeze test at catch height," SpaceX said in an X post today (Nov. 10). That post shared four photos of the giant booster, which is powered by 33 of SpaceX's next-gen Raptor engines. The first shot showed Super Heavy in one of Starbase's "Mega Bay" assembly buildings before rollout, while the other three depicted it grasped by the tower's arms, held high in the South Texas sky. SpaceX will try to catch both Super Heavy and Ship during Flight 15 — something it's never done before. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX has used the chopstick arms during Starship flights before; it has successfully caught Super Heavy on three separate occasions. But the company has never attempted a catch of Ship, which flies higher and farther than the booster and is therefore a more challenging target. And SpaceX only reached orbit with Starship for the first time on Flight 14, which launched on Sept. 28. So Flight 15 will break new ground. And, if all goes to plan, it will give us a look at the future: SpaceX plans to catch Super Heavy and Ship on all operational Starship missions, as this recovery strategy will allow the company to boost the megarocket's launch cadence. And SpaceX wants to fly Starship incredibly often, so that it can build out its Starlink V3 broadband constellation and even bigger Starmind AI data-center network . Indeed, Elon Musk has said the company is eyeing 10,000 Starship flights per year by 2030. The launch tower's "chopstick" arms giving the Flight 15 Super Heavy a loving squeeze. (Image credit: SpaceX) If all goes to plan, Flight 15 will launch from Starbase on Friday during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time). Super Heavy will return to Starbase for its catch about 6.5 minutes after liftoff. Ship will follow suit much later — about 22 hours later, in fact, after it has deployed 26 Starlink V3 spacecraft into LEO and completed 14 circuits of our planet. You can watch all the action live here at Space.com and get updates about the mission here .

Its planet-hopping space disaster narrative sees the crew of the starship Wild Blue Yonder hit a quantum anomaly, forcing their ship to crash-land onto a deadly exoplanet. All is not as it seems, though, as each crew member arrives in a different era on the same world. We hooked up with Mackie, DeBose, and Lequizamo to learn more about this renaissance of audio dramas and what attracted them to board Weir's sci-fi thriller. One crew. One planet. Three timelines. No one survives alone.
